start_collision_window_s.description: Opening seconds during which wall contact is treated as an artefact of where the robot was placed rather than a crash.  This exists because a legal starting cell may already sit against a wall. The starting square's middle band is only millimetres wider than the chassis, so a start there begins with almost no clearance to the inner block, and scoring that as a collision on tick one would fail a placement the rules allow.

start_collision_grace_s.description: How long such an opening contact may persist before it counts as a real failure rather than "still steering clear".

obstacles_inner_wall_terminal.description: Does inner-wall contact END an Obstacles run? In the RULES it does not. The rule set, operator-confirmed 2026-09-11: OPEN      -- the OUTER wall may not be touched (unchanged by this flag). BOTH      -- a wall may not be MOVED if it is not fixed, and moving one takes considerable force, which a scrape at this chassis's mass and speed does not reach. That is what makes relaxing this sound and not merely permitted. OBSTACLES -- the PARKING LOT may not be touched (9.24.7). Terminal regardless of this flag: the parking lot, displacing a sign out of its 85 mm circle (9.20), and the wrong pass side (9.19/9.24.5). Those three are the whole of what ends an Obstacles round. TRUE keeps the strict scoring every figure in this repo was measured under. Set FALSE to score the actual rule, and state which scoring a result used -- one taken under each and compared is meaningless.

lidar_invalid_ray_rate.description: Fraction of LIDAR rays OUTSIDE the chassis-occlusion bands that return no measurement, emitted as NaN/inf so the sanitising path the real driver uses is actually exercised. MEASURED 2026-09-14, no longer a placeholder: 5,763,600 rays from /scan over three of the 2026-09-13/14 hardware rounds give 9.5% outside the bands (25.4% over the whole sweep, but that figure is dominated by the bands and must not be applied uniformly). Was 0.01, a guess that understated the real rate by ~10x. It matters more than it looks: a dropout is substituted with MAX RANGE, which reads as "this side is wide open" to the direction estimator.

lidar_occlusion_min_deg.description: Inner edge, in degrees off the nose, of the two bands where the chassis occludes the LIDAR. Applied symmetrically, so the bands are [min, max] and [-max, -min]. MEASURED 2026-09-14 at 5 degree resolution over 5.76M real rays: dropout and sub-floor returns sum to essentially 100% across |bearing| 25-60 deg, i.e. the sensor returns nothing usable there at all, against 9.5% dropout and 0.13% sub-floor everywhere else. The edges 20-25 and 60-65 deg are partial (53-77% unusable) and are deliberately NOT modelled, so this is the conservative core of the effect. Note the config already declared blind wedges at +-120-160 deg for the REAR mount occlusion; these front bands were undeclared and unmodelled until now.

lidar_occlusion_max_deg.description: Outer edge, in degrees off the nose, of the chassis-occlusion bands. See lidar_occlusion_min_deg.

lidar_occlusion_dropout_rate.description: Fraction of rays inside an occlusion band that return nothing at all. MEASURED: of 1,120,700 real rays in |bearing| 25-60 deg, 68.9% were non-finite. The remaining 31.1% are chassis reflections, modelled by lidar_occlusion_self_return_m.

lidar_occlusion_self_return_m.description: Mean range of the chassis reflection seen inside an occlusion band. MEASURED: of the 31.1% of band rays that DO return, 99.7% read below min_valid_range_m (0.044), with p5 0.0108, p50 0.0207, p95 0.0280, min 0.0047, max 0.0435. This is the p50. These returns exist to exercise the min_valid_range_m filter, which is the whole point: the simulator used to clip every short ray to LIDAR_MIN_RANGE (0.045), and since 0.045 > 0.044 that made them survive the filter as valid 4.5 cm obstacles, the exact opposite of what the hardware does with them.

lidar_occlusion_self_return_std_m.description: Standard deviation of the chassis reflection range. MEASURED: derived from the p5-p95 span (0.0108 to 0.0280) of the real distribution, which is 3.29 sigma for a normal.

detection_confidence.description: Confidence stamped on emulated camera detections. Must stay above the sign router's min_confidence or no emulated detection would ever be accepted.

collision_margin_m.description: How far past the visual wall face TrackModel's chassis keep-out extends. Zero: the chassis may drive right up to the wall it can see, matching the real robot -- NOT the Go generator's fatter Gazebo collision mesh. See TrackModel's module docstring for the full reasoning.

axis_align_tolerance.description: |cos(yaw)| below this counts as a quarter-turn for ObstacleBox.from_pose.

no_progress_window_s.description: The simulator's no-progress bailout: a run is abandoned once the robot moves less than no_progress_displacement_m within no_progress_window_s. A HARNESS artefact, not a robot behaviour -- it ends a manoeuvre that is working but slow, which is exactly what the bay-exit ratchet looks like (diag_bay_start grew --no-progress-window for this). Written out 2026-09-05; both existed only as Python literals, at these same shipped values.

no_progress_displacement_m.description: Straight-line displacement (m) a run must net within no_progress_window_s or it is scored stuck.

vision_through_pinhole.description: Emulate camera BOUNDING BOXES and decode them with the shipped perception code, instead of handing the router world coordinates built from the TRUE range and bearing. Off, the simulator never runs _detection_to_world at all -- no pinhole, no bearing formula, no bbox-height gate, no aspect or frame-clip test -- all of which are live on the robot. That is how a MIRRORED camera bearing (fixed 2026-09-06) survived the 256-scenario corpus for weeks: the emulator reproduced the true geometry and the router's unit tests built their boxes by inverting the same formula, so both agreed with the error. The emulated box round-trips EXACTLY (1e-15 m) through the correct decode, so this is a wiring change rather than a noise source; with the historical mirror reintroduced it puts a sign 0.600 m onto the WRONG SIDE of a 1 m corridor. Ships false until the Obstacles corpus is re-baselined on it, since it changes which detections survive the discovery gates.

vision_range_model.description: Emulate detection RANGE falloff (not just geometry) on the emulated camera: a probit-ish falloff around R50, in metres.

min_turn_radius_tracks_speed.description: Floor the curvature at min(cap, intercept + slope * |v|) instead of the constant min_turn_radius_m. That constant is the curve's value at ONE speed: re-measured 2026-09-10 over 33 bags in free space at lock >= 30 deg, the achieved radius is 0.105 m at 0.025 m/s, 0.298 at 0.132 and saturates near 0.43 above 0.22, so 0.29 corresponds to ~0.118 m/s. The bay exit creeps end to end, where the constant is nearly 2x too large. The three constants live in robot.toml beside min_turn_radius_m; this only decides whether the simulator uses them. FALSE pending a corpus A/B -- it moves every contact- and corner-dependent number, exactly as shipping the constant floor did.

vision_detect_r50_m.description: Emulated camera range (m) at which a sign is detected on about half of frames.

vision_detect_falloff_m.description: Width (m) of the logistic detection-probability falloff around vision_detect_r50_m; smaller is a sharper cliff.

sensor_start_pos_error_m.description: Residual error (m) between where the robot is placed and where it believes it starts. MEASURED: post-626a011 the start pose is derived from the scan rather than assumed, and landed within 3.6-4.8 cm on all three real bags, so this is what survives the measurement rather than the old 0.35-0.80 m assumption. Non-zero implies use_lidar_localization, since sensor error is only observable through the estimate.

sensor_yaw_bias_rad.description: Constant heading offset (rad) between true and believed yaw. MEASURED on hardware. Until 2026-09-14 the whole simulation corpus ran with every sensor error at 0.0, i.e. a PERFECT pose and a perfect start placement, which is the easy side of every question that depends on the pose estimate.

sensor_imu_drift_rad_per_s.description: Heading drift rate (rad/s). The BNO085's quoted 0.5 deg/min.

sensor_gyro_scale_error.description: Fractional scale error on integrated yaw rate (0.005 = 0.5% long).

vision_latency_s.description: End-to-end delay (s) between a sign being visible and its detection reaching the navigator. MEASURED at 0.85 s on hardware -- the real gateway backs the pose up by exactly this before projecting a detection (sign_discovery.toml vision_latency_s). The simulator emitted from the CURRENT tick's true state until 2026-09-14, i.e. zero latency, which at 0.3 m/s hands the planner 0.26 m of anticipation it does not have on the mat.

vision_frame_miss_rate.description: Probability that an otherwise-visible sign produces NO detection on a given tick, on top of the range model. Hardware carries a detection on 11.6% of ticks (measured over 125 bags); the emulator with the range model alone carries one on ~54.5%. This closes that gap. It is a residual detector-miss term, not a camera frame-rate term: 15 fps against a 20 Hz control loop would only account for a quarter of it.

vision_color_flip_rate.description: Probability that a detection reports the OPPOSITE colour. UNMEASURED, so it ships at 0.0 rather than at a guess -- defaulting an invented error rate would make the simulator wrong in a new way rather than more realistic. The knob exists because colour confusion is the dominant real perception failure (the magenta parking barrier reaches the sign map as a RED pillar at p50 confidence 0.79) and the emulator copies ground-truth colour directly, so that entire failure mode is currently unscreenable. Needs a bag-derived confusion rate before it can ship non-zero.

vision_bearing_scatter_rad.description: Standard deviation of the per-detection camera BEARING error, in radians. The emulator projects every sign from its TRUE bearing, so the only angular error a simulated run carries is the pose estimate's -- and the camera's own scatter is an order of magnitude larger than that. MEASURED 2026-09-15 over 2,588 detections on the three rounds of that day whose pillar map reconstructs to the operator's stated layout: median +1.27 deg (so it is SCATTER, not a mountable offset), interquartile range -9.36 to +8.59 deg, giving a robust sigma of 13.30 deg = 0.232 rad. The raw standard deviation is 18.19 deg, inflated by outliers and by detections attributed to the wrong pillar, so the IQR-derived figure is the one to use. Why it matters: 0.232 rad at 1.5 m is 0.35 m of lateral miss, which is WIDER than sign_discovery.association_dist_m (0.25) and the router's detection_match_dist_m (0.30) -- the radii meant to contain it. A simulator without this cannot exercise the slot map, the colour vote's neighbour confusion, or any gate sized against that scatter. The measurement includes the localiser's yaw error, which the simulator already injects separately as sensor_yaw_bias_rad (0.03) and sensor_imu_noise_rad (0.005); together those are about 1.7 deg, so the double-count is under 2% of the figure. 0.0 reproduces the old idealised behaviour.

contact_slides_along_surfaces.description: Does a blocked translation SLIDE along the surface it hit, or is it scaled to nothing? The simulator scaled it to nothing until 2026-09-14, so a chassis meeting a wall at a shallow angle simply stopped dead instead of running along it: MEASURED 56x less progress at a 20 degree approach than a sliding model gives. That is not how a real chassis behaves against a smooth track wall, and because the bay exit is a sequence of shallow-angle contacts it voided every in-bay A/B taken before this. Set false to recover the old stop-dead behaviour.
